title: In 1 monkey, CCA-aligned M1 similarity at 2 to 3.3 years keeps 78% (post hoc; CI 61-105%) of its excess over a kinematics-only floor, while unaligned latents, tuning and fixed decoders decay
abstract: Question: do CCA-aligned latents of motor cortex stay similar beyond 2 years, while unaligned measures decay, and how much of the aligned similarity exceeds null floors? Data: LINK (DANDI 001201), one monkey, two Utah arrays in M1, 312 sessions over 1,242 days of finger movements without a decoder in the loop; spike-band power, 20-ms bins. Design: discovery (odd months) and held-out (even months) sessions; pipeline and thresholds fixed on discovery pairs of 365 days or less; predictions pre-registered with code hashes before the held-out run. Per pair, CCA on class-paired single-trial windows of 10-D PCA latents, cross-validated across trial folds; M1 = mean top-4 cross-validated canonical correlation. R730 = mean at gaps of 730 days or more / mean under 30 days; CIs from a bootstrap over 90-day blocks. Results (6,261 held-out pairs, 512 at 2.0-3.3 years): M1 is 0.914 at under 30 days and 0.888 at 2 years or more (R730 0.971 [0.955, 0.979]; pre-registered H1 supported). But H1 was a weak test: post hoc nulls give high and equally stable values: rotated movement labels 0.880, a kinematics-only surrogate with no neural data 0.834, disjoint electrode arrays 0.772, time-reversed data 0.771; all pass the H1 rule. Post hoc: above the kinematic floor the real data keep 0.78 [0.61, 1.05] of their 1-month excess (0.71-0.79 over other bin choices); above the time-reversal floor 0.84 [0.74, 0.92]. In the same pairs, unaligned latents keep 0.66 [0.56, 0.74], electrode tuning similarity 0.26 [0.13, 0.35], and an unaligned day-0 decoder falls to R^2 near 0. A day-0 decoder on aligned latents keeps 0.75 [0.54, 0.95] of its 1-month R^2 (pre-registered 70% test inconclusive). Thus class-related structure that CCA can align linearly is retained, at a level that is mostly expected from stable behaviour; this does not show stable intrinsic dynamics or the same units. Exploratory (post hoc): the part that tells true from rotated labels keeps 0.48 [0.36, 0.68] (90 deg) and 0.29 [0.13, 0.54] (180 deg); the kinematic surrogate has no such part. Exploratory: with half of the channels removed, M1 stays at 0.85-0.88. Threshold crossings: H1 holds, H1b inconclusive. Limitations: one animal; held-out pairs interleaved in time; 14 time blocks; floors are post hoc and depend on surrogate choices; recording and neural change cannot be separated.

display.caption: Held-out same-style pairs. A: aligned similarity M1 and its null floors (rotated labels, kinematics-only surrogate, disjoint electrodes, time reversal, shuffle), each divided by its mean at < 30 days; all pass the pre-registered H1 threshold. B: floor-corrected retention and the unaligned measures. C: decoder fixed on the earlier session, with and without alignment. Bands: 95% bootstrap over 90-day blocks.
Cross-validated correlation per canonical pair (aligned) or principal component (unaligned): only about 4 dimensions align reliably.

Exploratory. Left and middle: aligned similarity with one session's movement-class labels rotated; the label-specific part decreases at gaps of 2 years or more. Error bars are naive (too narrow). Right: simulated electrode loss on the later session.

citations.reason: LINK dataset (monkey N, Utah arrays, 312 sessions); all analyses use it.

Gallego et al. 2020: CCA-aligned latent dynamics stable for up to about 2 years. We use their alignment method and extend the measurement to 3.3 years in another monkey and task; null floors show that much of the aligned similarity is expected from stable behaviour.
Campaign paper on unaligned tuning similarity; its LINK tuning coefficients give the electrode-level similarity T for the same held-out pairs.

Hahn et al. 2026, Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain-computer interfaces over a 20-year period; campaign context and the tuning-similarity formula (its data are not used for results).
Nason et al. 2021: the two-finger task and setup of the LINK recordings.
Degenhart et al. 2020: BCI stabilisation by alignment of low-dimensional neural spaces (background).
LINK dataset code; used to understand the NWB fields.
Safaie et al. 2023: CCA-aligned latent dynamics are preserved across animals doing similar behaviour; the main reason to expect high aligned similarity from stable behaviour alone.
Elsayed and Cunningham 2017: population structure as an expected byproduct of simpler features; motivates the null floors.
Dabagia et al. 2023: alignment of latent representations of neural activity (related work).
Karpowicz et al. 2022: stabilizing BCIs by aligning latent dynamics (related work).
Farshchian et al. 2019: adversarial domain adaptation for stable brain-machine interfaces (related work).
Hahn et al. analysis code and summary tables (commit 93beb76): tuning-similarity formula and the range of the human tuning curves.
